project.name: starshell
project.description: A minimal, fast shell prompt with a fixed, hand-picked set of modules, built for Linux only.
project.relationship_to_upstream: starshell is a standalone fork of Starship (starship.rs): the source of a Starship release without what starshell does not ship, plus a short list of deliberate differences. Its version number mirrors the upstream release it was last reconciled against (currently 1.27.0); a matching number does not mean identical code, because code for modules this project does not ship is not carried. The `mould` section holds the rules that turn any upstream release into starshell's source tree, so a new release is ported by applying the mould to it and diffing the result against the repository; the maintainer runs it when a release is worth reconciling, it is not automatic. The scope rules, procedure, file map and registry of intentional differences for that reconciliation are in upstream_sync.
project.distribution: Binary only. No install script, no OS packages, no docs site, no CI/CD pipeline, no crates.io publishing.

upstream_sync.purpose: Self-contained instructions for producing starshell from upstream Starship and for reconciling a new upstream release into it. Read this section first, then `mould`, which holds the rules that turn any upstream release into starshell. Use core_engine, module_wiring_contract, modules, dependency_map and init_system as the reference for what exists in this tree and why. Two uses: (1) build -- apply `mould` to a clean copy of an upstream release to obtain the starshell source tree for it; (2) sync -- do that for a newer release and diff the result against the repository: that diff is the port. The mould is version-independent and is not rewritten per release; this section holds what changes per release: the baseline, the file map, the registry of intentional divergences and the reconciliation log.

upstream.release_notes: CHANGELOG.md at the repository root; the same text is on each GitHub release. Tags are named vX.Y.Z.
upstream.what_to_compare: A checkout (or source archive) of the target release tag, never main, so the diff matches the release notes. When several releases were skipped, read the notes of every release after the baseline, not only the latest.

baseline.meaning: Cargo.toml's version equals this release. Every upstream change up to and including it is either ported or listed as skipped in reconciliation_log. A change to starshell that is not a port of an upstream change must not move this number.

scope_rules.default: Parity. Everything upstream changes in code that starshell keeps arrives by applying the mould; only the mould's rules make starshell differ from upstream, each tagged with an entry of intentional_divergences. `principle`, `port` and `skip` below classify release-note items so that a reviewer can tell what to expect in the diff; they do not select what the mould does.
scope_rules.principle: A release-note item is relevant if and only if the files it changes, or the behaviour it fixes, exist in this tree. Verify by grepping this tree for the module, function or config key the item names -- do not infer from the item's title. Every item, ported or not, gets a line in reconciliation_log.
port: Security fixes in any file starshell contains (core engine, shipped modules, utils, init scripts) -- first, and with their tests.

Bug fixes and features of the 12 shipped modules (see modules.list) and their configs/<module>.rs structs. New config keys are added exactly as upstream spells them, so existing starship.toml files keep working.
Changes to the core engine: main.rs, lib.rs, config.rs, configure.rs, context.rs, module.rs, print.rs, segment.rs, logger.rs, bug_report.rs, formatter/, utils/, and all ten scripts in init/.
skip: Everything about a module that is not in modules.list: features, fixes, performance work, new modules (toolchain versions, cloud, containers, jj_*, vcs, battery, cmd_duration, env_var, hostname, sudo, ...).

Windows-only files, dependencies and build steps (modules/utils/directory_win.rs, deelevate, windows, winresource, the exe manifest). `#[cfg(windows)]` blocks inside files starshell keeps are not removed: they compile to nothing on Linux, and keeping them as upstream has them keeps diffs clean, so changes to them arrive unchanged.
Presets: the `preset` subcommand, preset files, and build.rs's preset-generation hook.
Everything outside src/, Cargo.toml and build.rs: documentation, install scripts, media, CI workflows, release automation, localisation, repository lint/typo/dependency-policy files.
Dependency-only churn in Cargo.toml -- see dependency_versions for when a bump is required instead.

naming_translation.rule: Upstream names are kept wherever possible so a diff against upstream stays readable. Only these differ.

map.crate and library name: upstream `starship` -> starshell `starshell` (Cargo [package] name; main.rs imports `starshell::...`; other files use `crate::`).
map.unchanged on purpose: the STARSHIP_* environment variables, starship.toml, the `::STARSHIP::` placeholder in init scripts, and every identifier in modules, configs and context -- see runtime_protocol.
map.git repo types (adopted from upstream in: GitRepo, GitRemote, Context::get_git_repo(), Context::git_repo -- identical to upstream; they replaced the earlier Repo / Remote / get_repo().

procedure: 1. Obtain the release notes for every release after baseline.last_reconciled_release and the source of the target tag (upstream.what_to_compare). Never modify the checkout; work on a copy.

2. Build the target: apply `mould` to a scratch copy of the target source (mould.how_to_use) and run its gates. Resolve every rule that failed, or went vacuous wrongly, as mould.when_a_rule_does_not_apply says. Apart from step 7, that is the only occasion on which the mould is edited.

3. Diff the built tree against the repository (src/, Cargo.toml, build.rs, LICENSE). That diff is the port. Triage its hunks against the release-note items with scope_rules and agree the port with the maintainer before changing the repository: every hunk must trace to an upstream change; a hunk that traces to nothing is a mould or repository error, to be resolved first.

4. Cargo.toml comes from the mould's template and does not follow upstream by itself: compare upstream's Cargo.toml at the baseline and target tags (compare_commands.upstream_changes) and apply mould.manifest_policy to the template.

5. Copy the built files into the repository. Regenerate Cargo.lock by building (the first build must not use --locked); only the starshell version line and genuinely changed dependencies should differ.

6. If a built hunk needs an API of a crate pinned behind upstream (dependency_versions), put the translation in the mould (a P6 rule, as D03 and D04), or bump that crate if the port genuinely needs the newer API. A fix must come with a test that fails without it: if upstream's test passes without the fix in starshell's harness, rewrite the test (precedent: D07). Run everything in `verification`.

7. When starshell adopts a deliberate new difference from upstream (a cut, an addition or a translation), add its rule to the mould and its entry to intentional_divergences in the same change; a difference without a rule does not survive the next release.

8. Update this file in the same change: project.version and cargo_toml.package_identity (the template's version follows the upstream release), baseline, file_map (re-run compare_commands.identical_check with UP at the target tag and move files between lists; each adapted entry's `rules` are the mould rules that touch the file), intentional_divergences (their `rules`), dependency_versions, a new reconciliation_log entry, and any core_engine / modules / dependency_map / known_footguns text the change made untrue. Then run mould.self_tests against the new baseline tag: both must pass.

compare_commands.note: Run from the starshell repository root. UP is the path of an upstream checkout; OLD and NEW are the baseline and target tags; BUILT is the tree the mould produced. identical_check compares starshell against whatever tag UP has checked out: at the baseline tag it verifies file_map before a sync, at the target tag it produces the new file_map after one.
compare_commands.upstream_changes: git -C "$UP" diff --stat vOLD vNEW -- src Cargo.toml build.rs
compare_commands.identical_check: for f in $(find src -type f ! -path 'src/test/fixtures/*' | sort) Cargo.toml build.rs; do if [ -f "$UP/$f" ]; then if cmp -s "$f" "$UP/$f"; then echo "identical  $f"; else echo "differs    $f"; fi; else echo "no-upstream $f"; fi; done
compare_commands.context_rs_note: src/context.rs has no upstream counterpart of that name: compare it against $UP/src/context/mod.rs and $UP/src/context/git_repo.rs (see D02).
compare_commands.port_diff: diff -r "$BUILT/src" src; for f in Cargo.toml build.rs LICENSE; do diff "$BUILT/$f" "$f"; done   # the output is the port; empty at the baseline

file_map.description: Where each starshell file stands relative to upstream at the baseline. `identical` files are byte-for-byte upstream: no rule of the mould touches them. `adapted` files differ only through the listed mould rules (`rules`), which implement the listed divergence ids. Upstream's own tree has more files than starshell; the ones that matter are listed under upstream_only.
upstream_only: src/modules/utils/directory_win.rs, src/modules/utils/format.rs, src/modules/utils/truncate.rs (see D07, D05, D12)
src/modules/<name>.rs and src/configs/<name>.rs for every module not in modules.list
build.rs's preset generation and everything outside src/ (see scope_rules.skip)
file_map.test_fixtures: src/test/fixtures/ holds git-repo.bundle and git-repo-sha256.bundle, which the git tests use, and hg-repo.bundle, which no test references (see unreconciled_deltas).

intentional_divergences.area: module scope: module.rs, modules/mod.rs, configs/mod.rs, configs/starship_root.rs
intentional_divergences.starshell: Only the shipped modules appear in ALL_MODULES, the `mod`/`pub mod` declarations, handle() and description() arms, FullConfig fields and PROMPT_ORDER. No `#[cfg(feature = "battery")]` items, no BatteryInfoProvider re-export. PROMPT_ORDER keeps upstream's relative order for the modules it contains. The `claude-code` default profile is `$git_branch`.
intentional_divergences.upstream: All upstream modules; the `claude-code` default profile is `$claude_model$git_branch$claude_context$claude_cost`.
intentional_divergences.when_porting: The mould filters these files down to the shipped modules, so upstream's hunks for shipped modules and for the generic machinery arrive by themselves, and a reordered PROMPT_ORDER keeps its new relative order. Never copy these files over by hand.

intentional_divergences.starshell: One file combining upstream's context/mod.rs and context/git_repo.rs, function for function and test for test. The GitRepo block is inserted above the `ScanDir` comment, and GitRemote is declared after the GitRepo impl block (upstream declares it between `struct GitRepo` and `impl GitRepo`). Omitted: context/jj_repo.rs, Context::jj_repo / set_jj_repo / get_jj_repo, the battery_info_provider field, Context::is_ssh_session (see D06). The doc comment and log message that say the git executable is used for `status and metrics` say `status` here, because git_metrics is not shipped.
intentional_divergences.upstream: A context/ directory with mod.rs, git_repo.rs and jj_repo.rs.
intentional_divergences.when_porting: Port a change to either upstream file into the matching place in context.rs. Skip anything that mentions JJRepo, jj or battery.

intentional_divergences.area: directory: Windows and the symlink test
intentional_divergences.starshell: modules/directory.rs imports directory_nix unconditionally as `directory_utils`; its `#[cfg(windows)]` blocks are otherwise upstream's. The test highlight_git_root_dir_symlinked_out_of_tree is #[ignore]d as upstream's is, but sets the canonical physical path with .path() and the symlink as the logical path with .logical_path(), which is what a real shell does.
intentional_divergences.upstream: Selects directory_nix or directory_win for `directory_utils` by target_os. Its version of the test passes the symlink as the physical path, and in starshell's harness that passes even without the fix because no repository is discovered.
intentional_divergences.when_porting: Keep the physical/logical form of the test. Directory tests that are #[ignore]d create files under $HOME; run them with a scratch HOME (verification).

intentional_divergences.starshell: main.rs imports `starshell::...`, uses the starshell bin name and `about` text; build.rs only calls shadow_rs::ShadowBuilder::builder().build().
intentional_divergences.upstream: `starship::...`, starship strings; build.rs also hooks preset generation and, on Windows, compiles a resource file.
intentional_divergences.when_porting: P6.8-P6.10 translate the names (naming_translation). build.rs is the template of P7.2: carry a change to upstream's shadow builder call into the template; the preset hook and the Windows block stay out.

intentional_divergences.starshell: No Preset type, preset_command, preset_list or `preset` subcommand and no presets directory; no env_var module, no Config::get_env_var_modules, no env_var branch in print.rs's handle_module and its implicit-module logic, and no `env_var` key allowance in utils/serde.rs (whose test uses [git_commit] where upstream uses [rust]); the module is absent from every wiring point as well (D01). build.rs has no preset generation.

intentional_divergences.starshell: Package name, authors, description and no crates.io metadata (documentation, homepage, include, keywords, categories, readme, repository). `default = []`; only the config-schema feature. Dependency set is the subset the shipped code uses (see dependency_map). No Windows dependency tables, no build-dependency on dunce. gix lists the zlib-rs feature (upstream's list does not). The release profile sets panic = "abort" (upstream's does not). The dev-dependency `mockall` (=0.15.0) is kept although nothing in src/ references it; upstream uses it only for the battery module's tests.
intentional_divergences.upstream: Full metadata; default features battery and notify; the dependency set of every module; Windows tables.
intentional_divergences.when_porting: The manifest is the template of P7.1 (mould.manifest_policy). Add a dependency to it only if kept code references it (check dependency_map). Do not copy features or Windows tables. Version requirements: see dependency_versions.

intentional_divergences.starshell: ModuleRenderer and fixture_repo support git only: FixtureProvider has the single variant Git; the HG_FIXTURE constant is gone, but src/test/fixtures/hg-repo.bundle stays in the repository although no test uses it. The `git_trust` builder sits directly after `logical_path`.
intentional_divergences.upstream: Also JJTester / jj_repo(), Hg, Fossil, Jujutsu and Pijul fixture providers, an HG_FIXTURE constant, and a battery provider hook; `git_trust` sits before `logical_path`.

intentional_divergences.starshell: Upstream's repository tooling and lint-policy files are not carried over (mould rule P2.1 keeps only LICENSE, build.rs, Cargo.toml and src at the root; README.md and Cargo.lock are starshell's own). lib.rs and main.rs still contain upstream's crate-level `#![warn(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`, and create_command() in utils/mod.rs keeps its single `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` on Command::new, but with no lint policy configured that lint never fires, so neither line has an effect.

dependency_versions.policy: Cargo.toml version requirements are not kept in step with upstream; Cargo.lock pins what actually builds. The three crates below cross a breaking boundary and are why ported code needs translating. All other requirements are at most patch or minor releases behind within the same major series. The Cargo.toml template (mould P7.1) carries these requirements and the translations are mould rules (P6, D03 and D04): a release that needs a newer requirement changes the template, not the built tree.

behind_upstream_at_baseline.consequence: none observed: dirs is called at three sites (dirs::config_dir in bug_report.rs, dirs::cache_dir in logger.rs, dirs::home_dir in utils/mod.rs) and all three compile against both majors

dependency_versions.when_a_bump_is_required: A ported hunk does not compile against the pinned version, or a security advisory names the pinned version. Bump only that crate, re-run verification, remove its entry above and its translation from intentional_divergences.

other_changes: Cargo.toml version 0.1.0 -> 1.27.0: the version now mirrors the reconciled upstream release (project.relationship_to_upstream).
architecture.json gained the `mould`: version-independent rules that turn any upstream release (1.26.0 and later) into starshell's source tree, and reproduce this release byte for byte.

mould.purpose: The mould that turns any upstream Starship release into starshell. Apply it to a clean copy of the upstream source of release R and the result is starshell's source tree for R. Applied to the baseline release it reproduces src/, Cargo.toml, build.rs and LICENSE of this repository byte for byte; applied to a newer release it yields the tree starshell would have if every upstream change to code starshell keeps had been ported, so the difference between that result and the repository is the port (upstream_sync.procedure). The mould is not rewritten per release: its rules name code items (functions, structs, impl blocks, match arms, fields), never line numbers, so they find their targets wherever upstream moves them.
mould.formula: starshell(R) = canonicalise( templates + upstream(R) - cuts + additions + translations ). templates: Cargo.toml and build.rs (P7). cuts: files, module wiring, the context/ directory merge and unshipped code (P2-P5). additions and translations: P1 and P6. canonicalise: P8.
principle: Parity by default: upstream code that no rule names flows through unchanged. Every upstream fix, feature and refactor in code starshell keeps therefore arrives by itself when the mould is applied to a newer release; nothing is ported by hand.

Deny by default in exactly two places: which modules exist (src/modules and src/configs keep only parameters.shipped_modules, P2.2-P2.3) and what sits at the repository root (only LICENSE, build.rs, Cargo.toml and src, P2.1). A module, config or top-level file that upstream adds later is dropped without any rule being written.

Every other difference from upstream is a rule, tagged with the divergence it implements (`div`; upstream_sync.intentional_divergences). A difference that no rule produces must not exist in the repository.

Rules are anchored by symbol, not by position: a rule names the item it acts on (fn, struct, enum, impl, mod, use, const, static, field, variant, match arm) and the container it sits in. A rule whose target does not exist in a release is vacuous, not an error: there is nothing to cut or translate there.

Rules are idempotent: a rule either finds its target in upstream's form, finds nothing, or (rules that add text) carries an `unless` guard. Applying the mould to starshell's own files changes nothing: starshell is a fixed point of the mould (self_tests T2).
mould.input: The source of upstream release R: a release source archive, `git archive` output of tag vR, or the crates.io source package of starship R. Always work on a copy in an empty scratch directory: the rules delete, move and rewrite files, and P2.1 deletes every entry at the root that is not kept, hidden ones such as .git included.
mould.output: starshell's src/, Cargo.toml, build.rs and LICENSE for release R. Nothing else in the repository is produced.

not_derived.README.md: Written by hand for starshell (fork notice, why the fork exists, the table of the twelve modules, build and license notes). P2.1 deletes upstream's README; the repository's stays.
not_derived.Cargo.lock: Generated, not derived. Copy the repository's Cargo.lock next to the built Cargo.toml before P8, so cargo resolves the dependency versions starshell is known to build with; afterwards only the starshell version line and genuinely changed dependencies may differ. Build without --locked the first time.

how_to_use: 1. Copy the upstream source of release R into an empty scratch directory (mould.input).

2. Apply the phases P1 to P7 in order and the rules of each phase in listed order; every rule sees the files as the earlier rules left them. For each rule find its target as rule_semantics describes, apply it, and record `applied`, `vacuous` or `failed`. P1 must come before P2, because P2 deletes the file P1 copies from.
3. When a rule fails, or is vacuous where the gates later show it should not have been, follow when_a_rule_does_not_apply before going on. Never skip an edit that is still needed.

4. P8: copy the repository's Cargo.lock into the scratch directory and run its commands there, in order. A compile error here means a rule is missing or no longer fits the release (when_a_rule_does_not_apply).
5. Run the gates on the result.

6. Compare the scratch directory's src/, Cargo.toml, build.rs and LICENSE with the repository. The difference is the port of everything upstream changed since the baseline in code starshell keeps; upstream_sync.procedure continues from here.

parameters.note: Must equal the names in modules.list. `$shipped_modules` in a rule stands for this list. `{upstream_version}` in the Cargo.toml template (P7.1) stands for the `version` of [package] in upstream's Cargo.toml (for a crates.io source package, the version line of its Cargo.toml).

rule_semantics.model: A rule is a JSON object: `id`, `op` (what to do), `div` (the divergence id or ids it implements), the operands of the op and `intent` (what the result must look like, in words). When the mechanical form of a rule does not fit a release, achieve its `intent`.
rule_semantics.files: Paths are relative to the root of the scratch directory; text is UTF-8 with `\n` line ends and every file ends with one newline. Rules that name items work on whole lines: an element's first line is the line of its first attribute or comment.

locators.item: `fn`, `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait`, `mod`, `const`, `static`, `type` followed by the identifier, e.g. `fn get_git_repo`, `struct Context`, `mod tests`. Only direct children of the container are searched. A function declared several times under different #[cfg] attributes matches every declaration.
locators.use: `use <path>`: the `use` declaration whose path, from after `use` to before `;` with whitespace normalised, equals <path> exactly, e.g. `use super::utils::directory_win as directory_utils`.
locators.impl: `impl <Type>` or `impl <Trait> for <Type>`: every impl block whose header (the generic parameter list after `impl` removed, whitespace normalised) equals the text or starts with it followed by `<` or a space. `impl Context` matches `impl Context {` and `impl<'a> Context<'a> {`, not `impl ContextFoo`.
locators.field, variant: `field <name>` / `variant <name>`: a member of the struct / enum that is the container.
locators.arm: `arm <pattern>`: a match arm whose pattern text (before `=>`, a guard included) equals <pattern> or starts with it followed by a character that cannot continue a path: `arm Commands::Preset` matches `Commands::Preset { .. } =>`, `arm "git_branch"` matches `"git_branch" => ...`. Arms are searched in every `match` inside the container, nested matches included.

common_fields.in: Container path, outermost first: a list of locators, each searched in the body of the one before (the first in the whole file). A step that matches several elements, such as several `impl Context` blocks, stands for all of them. Without `in`, targets are searched among the top-level items of the file.
common_fields.occurrence: When a `target` matches several elements: 1 is the first, -1 the last. `anchor_occurrence` does the same for `relative_to`.
common_fields.unless: A text. If the rule's file already contains it, the rule is vacuous (already satisfied).
common_fields.count: On `edit` and `regex`: the exact number of replacements the rule must make; a different positive number makes the rule fail.

rule_semantics.element: An element is a whole item, field, variant or arm: the attributes (`#[...]`) and comment lines directly above it with no blank line between (a `//!` comment does not attach), the item up to its closing brace or `;`, and, for fields, variants and arms, the trailing `,`.
rule_semantics.blank_lines: Deleting or moving an element removes whole lines. A blank line that the removal would leave doubled, directly after an opening bracket, or directly before a closing bracket is dropped. `cargo fmt` (P8) normalises everything else.

outcomes.vacuous: The rule's file, container, target or text does not exist in this release, or its `unless` text is present: nothing to do. Expected: most rules are vacuous on a release that lacks the code they cut. A vacuous rule is wrong only when a gate then shows what it should have handled (when_a_rule_does_not_apply).
outcomes.failed: The target exists but the rule cannot be applied as written: a locator that must match one element matches several, a `count` differs, or a file does not parse.

ops.delete: Delete the elements named by `target` (one locator) or `targets` (several), inside `in` if given; with `match` {kind, name, body} instead, every direct child of the container whose kind is `kind`, whose name contains a match of the regex `name` and whose text contains a match of the regex `body`. A locator that matches several elements fails unless `all` is true.
ops.replace: Replace the one element named by `target` with the lines of `with`.
ops.insert: Insert the lines of `lines` as a block `where` = before | after the element named by `relative_to`, with one blank line between block and element.
ops.move: Take the element named by `target` out of its place and put it before | after (`where`) the element named by `relative_to`, with one blank line between them.
ops.inline_items: Copy the items named in `items` from the file `from` (as it is before P2 deletes it); with `private`, drop each item's leading `pub` / `pub(..)`; for each pair in `rename` rename `fn <old>` and every call `<old>(` that is not preceded by a word character, `.` or `:`; join the items with one blank line and insert them like `insert` does (`relative_to`, `where`).
ops.edit: Replace the exact text `old` by `new` in the file, or only inside the element named by the last locator of `in` (that element must be unique). A list for `old` or `new` stands for its lines joined with newlines.
ops.regex: As `edit`, with the regular expression `pattern` (Python `re` syntax; `flags`: s = `.` matches newline, m = `^` and `$` match at every line, i = ignore case) and a replacement `repl` that may use \1 back-references.
ops.strip_attr: Delete the line that is exactly `attr` from the attributes of the element named by `target`.
ops.delete_cfg_gated: In every .rs file under src/ delete each element (item, field, variant, statement or initialiser) that carries the attribute `attr`, together with the attribute; a field, initialiser or statement runs to its terminating `,` or `;`. Repeat until none is left.
ops.keep_arms: In the function named by `in`, keep only the arms of the first `match` in its body whose pattern text (quotes included) fully matches one of the regexes of `keep`, ordered by the first regex they match (arms that match the same regex keep upstream's order), directly one under the other without blank lines; delete the other arms.
ops.delete_path: Delete the file or directory `path`; absent: vacuous.
ops.keep_only: In the directory `dir` delete every entry, hidden ones included, whose name is not in `keep` (each name followed by `suffix` when given) or `also_keep`.
ops.write_file: Create or overwrite `path` with `lines` joined with newlines plus a final newline; then replace each key of `substitute` in the text by the value its description gives.
ops.merge_module_dir: Combine the directory module `dir` (mod.rs and sibling files) into the single file `into`: start from dir/mod.rs, delete every `mod X;` / `pub mod X;` declaration and every `use X::...;` re-export whose X is a sibling file; then for each sibling file not listed in `cut`, in file-name order, insert its items (everything from its first item that is not a `use` to its last item) directly above the element `anchor`, with one blank line between block and anchor; write the result to `into` and delete `dir`. The siblings' own `use` lines are not copied: imports that the merged items need and `into` lacks are added by rules (P4.2) or, when a release needs more, by hand (when_a_rule_does_not_apply). When `dir` does not exist the rule is vacuous: the release still has the single file.
ops.filter_string_array: In `file`, the array that starts at the line beginning `pub const <array>` and ends at the first later line equal to `];` keeps only the lines of the form `"name",` (leading whitespace allowed) whose name is in `keep`, in their original order. The opening and closing lines stay; every other line between them (attributes, comments, names not kept) is removed.
ops.filter_mod_declarations: In `file`, every unindented line `mod name;` or `pub mod name;` whose name is in neither `keep` nor `always_keep` is removed, together with the run of attribute lines (lines starting `#[`) directly above it. Other lines, `pub use` lines included, are untouched.
ops.filter_match_arms: In `file`, inside `pub fn <fn>`, find the line `match module {`. Its arms sit one indentation level deeper. An arm starts at a line `"name" =>` or `<identifier> if <condition> =>`, together with the attribute lines at that indentation directly above it, and runs up to the line before the next arm or before the closing brace of the match; the continuation lines of a multi-line arm belong to it. Keep an arm when its name is in `keep`, when its identifier is in `always_keep_guards`, or when it is the default arm `_ =>`; remove every other arm. Comment lines before the first arm stay.
ops.filter_struct_fields: In `file`, in `pub struct <struct>`, after the line whose trimmed text equals `after_comment`, remove every field line `    name: ...` (four spaces) whose name is not in `keep`, together with the attribute lines directly above it. All other lines stay.

when_a_rule_does_not_apply.when: A rule is vacuous because upstream dropped, or never had, the code it cuts or translates, and the gates show nothing left over.
when_a_rule_does_not_apply.then: Nothing. The rule stays in the mould for the releases that still have the code.

when_a_rule_does_not_apply.when: A gate shows a leftover (a residue token, an unresolved import, an unknown field, a compile error) and the rule that should have handled it is vacuous or failed.
when_a_rule_does_not_apply.then: Upstream renamed, moved or rewrote the item. Find its new form in the upstream source, re-target the rule (its locator or its text) so that it keeps its `intent`, and apply it. Re-targeting is the usual reason for editing an existing rule.

when_a_rule_does_not_apply.when: An `edit`, `regex` or `replace` rule fails because upstream changed the text it matches.
when_a_rule_does_not_apply.then: Achieve the rule's `intent` on the new text by hand, then change the rule's text to match the new upstream so that it applies mechanically next time.

when_a_rule_does_not_apply.when: Upstream adds code in a kept file that depends on something starshell cuts (a use of Preset, env_var, a battery gate, JJRepo, ...), shown by the residue gate or by a compile error.
when_a_rule_does_not_apply.then: Add a cut rule to P5 that names the new item (a `delete`, or a `delete_cfg_gated` for a new feature gate), tagged with the divergence it belongs to. Add a divergence entry only when none describes the feature.

when_a_rule_does_not_apply.when: Built code does not compile against a crate that starshell pins behind upstream (dependency_versions).
when_a_rule_does_not_apply.then: Add a translation rule to P6 in the manner of D03 and D04, or bump the crate under dependency_versions.when_a_bump_is_required.

when_a_rule_does_not_apply.when: self_tests T1 or T2 fail on the repository you started from.
when_a_rule_does_not_apply.then: The mould and the repository were edited independently. Decide which one is right and change the other; never leave both.

mould.manifest_policy: Cargo.toml and build.rs are starshell's own files, written by P7 from templates; the Cargo.toml template carries `{upstream_version}`. Upstream's Cargo.toml is read for three things only: its version; changes to the requirement of a crate the template already lists (the pins that deliberately stay behind are in dependency_versions); and a crate that kept code newly needs. Features, Windows tables and crates.io metadata are never carried over (D10). Compare upstream's manifest between the baseline and the target with compare_commands.upstream_changes.

verified_on.result: All 78 rules apply and P8 succeeds. src/, Cargo.toml, build.rs and LICENSE come out byte-identical to the repository (69 files). Applying the mould to the repository's own files changes nothing: 22 rules rewrite identical text and 56 are vacuous (self_tests T1 and T2).

core_engine.definition: Everything in src/ except modules/*.rs and configs/*.rs. This is the part of the codebase that changes for reasons unrelated to which modules exist: CLI behavior, config parsing, prompt assembly, formatting, git/repo discovery infrastructure.

files.main.rs: Binary entry point. Defines the CLI (clap-based) and dispatches it. Subcommands: prompt, module, explain, timings, time, session, init, completions, config, print-config, toggle, bug-report, statusline (the claude-code provider only), and config-schema (only built with the config-schema feature). There is no `preset` subcommand. Imports the library crate as `starshell::...`; the bin name and `about` text are starshell-specific.
files.lib.rs: Library crate root. Declares all top-level modules, invokes shadow_rs's `shadow!` macro for build metadata (PKG_VERSION, CLAP_LONG_VERSION), and exposes thread-count helpers driven by the STARSHIP_NUM_THREADS env var.
files.config.rs: Loads and parses starship.toml. Exposes get_custom_modules() for reading the [custom.*] table, and generic get_config()/get_module_config() lookups used throughout.
files.context.rs: The Context struct: current directory, environment snapshot, shell/target info, and the core git repo-discovery machinery (gix-based GitRepo/get_git_repo(), shared by directory.rs, custom.rs's require_repo option, and every git_* module). GitRepo records the repository's trust level (gix git_dir_trust): exec_git runs the git executable only in fully trusted repositories, exec_git_with_required_trust lets a caller accept reduced trust for fixed ref queries that cannot run repository-configured filters or hooks, and use_git_executable()/uses_reftables() decide when git_status/git_branch may shell out to git at all (at reduced trust git_status falls back to gix). Also owns the generic detect_env_vars/detect_env_vars2 mechanism used by username and python to conditionally activate based on environment variables being present -- this is unrelated to any module named 'env_var'; no such module exists in this project.
files.module.rs: Defines ALL_MODULES (the authoritative list of statically-dispatched module names) and the Module struct/segment-rendering primitives.
files.modules/mod.rs: Dispatches a module name to its implementation via handle(), and supplies one-line descriptions via description(). custom is dispatched dynamically by "custom." prefix match, not by exact name, so it does not appear in ALL_MODULES.
files.configs/mod.rs: Defines FullConfig, the aggregate struct combining the root prompt config with every module's config struct. Drives starship.toml parsing and (optionally) JSON-schema generation.
files.configs/starship_root.rs: Defines StarshipRootConfig (format, right_format, palettes, profiles, etc.) and PROMPT_ORDER, the default module rendering order used only when a user's format string is "$all".
files.print.rs: Assembles the final prompt string: resolves the format string against PROMPT_ORDER or an explicit format, expands "$custom" into every configured [custom.*] entry via handle_module()/should_add_implicit_module(), and renders styled segments.
files.configure.rs: Implements `starshell config` (opening the config file in $EDITOR) and related config-editing subcommands.
files.formatter/: The format-string parser and renderer. spec.pest defines the grammar; string_formatter.rs and parser.rs implement it; version.rs provides shared version-string formatting used by python (via versions crate) and time.
files.init/: Shell integration. init/mod.rs unconditionally embeds every script in this directory via include_str!() and dispatches by the CompletionShell enum / Commands::Init match arms in main.rs -- see init_system.critical_invariant below.
files.utils/: utils/mod.rs: command execution (create_command, exec_cmd, mock_cmd for tests), bounded file reading (read_file: regular files only, 100 MiB cap, non-blocking open), write_file / write_file_atomic, shell escape-sequence wrapping, home_dir. utils/env.rs: the Env wrapper over environment variables, with a HashMap mock under cfg(test). utils/serde.rs: custom serde deserializer enforcing the allowed top-level TOML key set. utils/statusline.rs: the Claude Code statusline JSON structs.
files.segment.rs: Styled text segment primitive used by every module's rendering output.
files.modules/utils/: Helpers shared by shipped modules: directory.rs (path truncation), directory_nix.rs (write-permission check via nix, for the directory module's read-only symbol), path.rs (PathExt). No directory_win.rs, format.rs or truncate.rs -- see upstream_sync D05, D07.
files.statusline: Claude Code status line support, spread over several files: `starshell statusline claude-code` (main.rs) calls print::prompt_with_claude_code, which deserializes Claude Code's JSON from stdin into utils/statusline.rs's ClaudeCodeData (all structs #[serde(default)], unknown keys ignored), stores it in Context.claude_code_data (context.rs), and renders the profile named `claude-code` from configs/starship_root.rs (default `$git_branch`). No shipped module reads claude_code_data.
files.test/: Test-only support (mod.rs): ModuleRenderer, default_context(), git fixture repositories built from the .bundle files in test/fixtures/, and the git trust-level builder. Only built under cfg(test).
files.bug_report.rs: Implements `starshell bug-report`; the only consumer of the urlencoding crate and one of several consumers of os_info (for OS/version info in the report body, independent of whether the os module is enabled).

module_wiring_contract.description: A statically-dispatched module must be registered consistently in exactly four places, all agreeing on the same string name. custom is the one exception: it is dispatched dynamically by prefix match and does not appear in ALL_MODULES or PROMPT_ORDER's module-name test, though it does appear in PROMPT_ORDER for default-ordering purposes and has its own field-shape (an IndexMap, not a single struct) in FullConfig.

points.must_be: Alphabetically sorted (enforced by a test in this file). Contains every statically-dispatched module name.

points.construct: mod <name>; + match arm in handle() + entry in description()
points.must_be: One line per point per module, kept alphabetical by convention (not enforced by a compiler test beyond description() coverage).
A field whose type is the module's Config struct (or an IndexMap<String, Config> for dynamically-named instances like custom).
Only affects default rendering when format = "$all". A module can be fully wired and functional while absent from this list; it just won't appear under the default format.

compiler_enforced_checks: module.rs: test_all_modules_is_in_alphabetical_order -- fails if ALL_MODULES drifts from sorted order.
configs/mod.rs: test_all_modules_in_full_config -- fails if any name in ALL_MODULES is missing as a key in FullConfig's serialized form.
module_wiring_contract.not_compiler_enforced: Nothing checks that PROMPT_ORDER matches ALL_MODULES, or that modules/mod.rs's description() entries match ALL_MODULES exactly (the all_modules_have_description test only checks descriptions aren't the placeholder string, not that every ALL_MODULES entry has a *custom* one).

list.name: directory
list.purpose: Displays the current working directory, with truncation and path substitution rules.

list.name: git_branch
depends_on: context::GitRepo (uses_reftables(); exec_git_with_required_trust at reduced trust for its fixed symbolic-ref/for-each-ref queries) -- no cross-module imports

list.name: git_commit
list.purpose: Displays the active commit hash / tag.

list.name: git_state
list.purpose: Displays the current git operation in progress (rebase, merge, etc.) and its step.

list.name: git_status
list.purpose: Displays working-tree status counts (staged, modified, untracked, ahead/behind, etc.). Declared `pub` (not just `mod`) in modules/mod.rs; its only remaining out-of-module consumer is test-only (context.rs's tests call git_status::tests::make_sparse).
depends_on: context::GitRepo (use_git_executable() decides whether the git executable may be used for status; exec_git_with_required_trust at reduced trust for its for-each-ref upstream query)

list.name: time
list.purpose: Displays the current local time in a configurable format.

list.name: character
list.purpose: Displays the prompt character/arrow, styled by last command success/failure.

list.name: os
list.purpose: Displays an icon (and optionally name/version/codename) for the detected OS or Linux distribution. Disabled by default; must be explicitly enabled with `disabled = false` and referenced in a format string to render anything. Ships a built-in symbol table covering ~60 distros/platforms recognized by os_info, overridable per-entry in [os.symbols].
depends_on: os_info crate (already required independently by bug_report.rs)

list.name: python
list.purpose: Displays the active Python version / virtualenv name.

list.name: line_break
list.purpose: Inserts a line break in multi-line prompt formats.

list.name: custom
list.dispatch: dynamic ("custom.<name>" prefix match; also expands bare "$custom" in a format string to every configured [custom.*] entry via print.rs's handle_module/should_add_implicit_module)
list.purpose: Runs a user-specified shell command and displays its output as a segment. Supports gating by detected files/extensions/folders, an arbitrary `when` shell condition, `require_repo`, and OS filtering. The general-purpose mechanism for displaying anything not covered by a dedicated module.

not_present.description: Modules from upstream Starship that do not exist in this codebase at all -- no file, no wiring, nothing to remove or disable. Re-adding any of these means copying the module/config file pair from an upstream checkout and wiring all four points above, then verifying no other file (grep the whole tree, not just the module's own filename) has orphaned helper functions whose only purpose was serving that module.

Removed after python and username's existing detect_env_vars/detect_env_vars2 activation mechanism was judged sufficient and custom was judged capable of covering any remaining ad-hoc display need.

examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.name: shell
examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.reason: Displays detected shell name; not depended on by any module in this list.

examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.name: status
examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.reason: Displays last command exit code; not depended on by any module in this list.

examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.name: cmd_duration
examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.reason: Displays command elapsed time. Its removal is also why notify-rust and two small formatting helpers (elapsed-time humanizer, integer humanizer) do not exist in utils/mod.rs.

examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.name: vcs
examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.reason: Meta-dispatcher to whichever VCS is detected; not depended on by any module in this list, and nothing in this list depends on it either.

examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.name: jj_bookmark / jj_change / jj_metrics / jj_status
examples_considered_and_intentionally_ex.reason: Jujutsu modules (plus Jujutsu support inside vcs) added upstream in 1.27.0. No Jujutsu support is shipped: vcs is excluded and nothing in this list depends on them.

not_present.everything_else: All other upstream modules (toolchain/language version modules, cloud-provider modules, container/orchestration modules, etc.) are simply absent -- not disabled, not stubbed, no trace in the wiring files.

dependency_map.description: Each entry lists every file in src/ that references the crate, verified by direct grep against the current tree. A crate with a single consumer is a strong signal that removing that consumer should prompt removing the crate too.

nu-ansi-term: and most modules for styled output
schemars: config.rs, every configs/*.rs, print.rs -- optional, gated behind the config-schema feature
serde / serde_json: config.rs, every configs/*.rs, utils/serde.rs, utils/statusline.rs, print.rs
shadow-rs: lib.rs (via the shadow! macro, not path syntax) -- provides PKG_VERSION/CLAP_LONG_VERSION; build.rs also depends on it as a build-dependency
toml / toml_edit: config.rs, configure.rs, most modules' tests, configs/mod.rs
mockall: (dev-dependency; no file in src/ references it)

not_present.description: Crates absent from Cargo.toml because nothing in this tree references them. Re-adding a module that needs one of these means re-adding the crate too.

init_system.description: Shell integration for bash, zsh, fish, elvish, nushell, tcsh, xonsh, powershell, and ion. Each shell's init snippet is a static file in src/init/, embedded into the binary at compile time.
init_system.critical_invariant: src/init/mod.rs includes every one of these files via include_str!() completely unconditionally -- there is no #[cfg] gate keyed on platform or shell choice. Shell selection happens at runtime via `starshell init <shell>`, dispatched through the CompletionShell enum and Commands::Init match arms in main.rs, not through compile-time branching. Deleting any file this module includes breaks the build on every platform, regardless of whether that shell 'belongs' to the platform you're targeting. To drop support for a shell, you must remove it from three places in lockstep: the CompletionShell enum, the relevant match arms in main.rs, and the include_str!/const declaration in init/mod.rs -- deleting only the script file is not sufficient and will not compile.
init_system.upstream_parity: As of 1.27.0 all ten scripts are byte-identical to upstream Starship's, so a plain diff against an upstream checkout shows only genuine upstream changes.

runtime_protocol.description: User-facing names and file conventions, deliberately kept identical to upstream Starship for drop-in compatibility with existing shell configurations, independent of the starshell package/binary rename.
runtime_protocol.config_file: starship.toml, located via the STARSHIP_CONFIG environment variable or the platform default config path.
runtime_protocol.cli_program_name: starshell (the compiled binary name and the name embedded into generated shell completions -- this one detail was changed from upstream, everything else in this section was not)

cargo_toml.package_identity: name = starshell, version = 1.27.0 (mirrors the upstream release last reconciled -- see project.relationship_to_upstream). No documentation/homepage/repository/include/readme/categories/keywords fields -- these only matter for `cargo package`/crates.io publishing, which this project never does.

features.default: empty -- no features enabled by default
features.config-schema: optional, gated on the schemars dependency; enables `starshell config-schema` to emit a JSON schema for FullConfig

release_profile.rationale: Tuned for a binary built rarely but executed on every shell prompt render: maximize runtime speed and minimize size at the cost of build time. panic=abort applies only to this profile; `cargo test` builds under a separate profile and retains normal unwinding.

known_footguns.risk: Assuming a shell's init script can be deleted because its target platform doesn't match your build target. See init_system.critical_invariant -- include_str! calls in init/mod.rs are unconditional.

Deleting a module's own two files (modules/<name>.rs, configs/<name>.rs) and its four wiring points is necessary but not sufficient. Other files may contain helper functions, test fixtures, or allowlist entries that existed solely to support that module (precedent: a dead test-fixture table in utils/mod.rs, a dead helper function in config.rs, a stale entry in utils/serde.rs's allowed-top-level-key check, all discovered only by grepping for the module's name/type across the whole tree, not just checking whether its own two files still compile).

A module's Cargo.toml dependency may already be present for an unrelated reason (os_info was already required by bug_report.rs before the os module was re-added). Check the dependency_map before assuming a crate needs to be added; check it again before assuming one should be removed.

An #[allow(dead_code)] does not mean the code is legitimately used elsewhere for a reason clippy can't see -- it can just as easily mean a function has been orphaned and nobody removed the allow along with its last caller. Precedent: utils/mod.rs had a #[cfg(test)]/#[cfg(not(test))] pair of context_path() functions, each individually marked #[allow(dead_code)], with zero callers anywhere in the tree (test or production) once verified by grep. The allow had been silently hiding this since it predates this fork. Do not treat the presence of #[allow(dead_code)] as evidence the code is needed -- grep for real callers before trusting it, the same way you would for any other function.

Before trusting the tree, grep for every #[allow(...)], #![allow(...)], and #[warn(...)] site and check each individually -- do not assume a suppression is still contextually valid just because it was valid when written. Most in this codebase are legitimate and narrowly scoped (test-only struct fields with no reader by design, generated-code lint false positives from pest_derive, platform-conditional numeric conversions with an inline comment explaining why). One category is worth extra scrutiny every time: any #[allow(dead_code)] on a pub fn, since that is exactly the lint that would otherwise catch an orphaned function left over from a deleted module or a refactor. std::process::Command::new is called only from utils/mod.rs's create_command() -- confirm it remains the *only* call site (grep 'Command::new') if you ever touch process-spawning code.

Run git only through GitRepo::exec_git (requires full repository trust) or GitRepo::exec_git_with_required_trust. Accept reduced trust only for fixed commands whose arguments cannot make git run repository-configured filters or hooks (today: symbolic-ref and for-each-ref in git_branch.rs and git_status.rs). `git status` runs at full trust only; at reduced trust git_status falls back to gix. A new exec_git caller must decide its trust requirement deliberately.

Read files through utils::read_file, never fs::read_to_string, fs::read or Read::read_to_string on a path that depends on the current directory or repository contents: read_file refuses non-regular files (a FIFO cannot hang the prompt) and files over 100 MiB. When touching file-reading code, grep for fs::read_to_string, fs::read and read_to_string to confirm nothing bypasses it. Known exception, deliberately left as upstream has it: modules/python.rs reads pyvenv.cfg with Ini::load_from_file_noescape, whose path comes from the user-set VIRTUAL_ENV rather than from repository contents.
